clue.text: Rail merger on the table

explanation.surface: A railway company merger being discussed at the boardroom table.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two pieces, FISH PLATE is a dish for serving fish at the table, while the hyphenated word is the metal bar that joins two lengths of railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail-joining bar bolted across two rail ends unites them; a serving dish for seafood sits on a dining table.

clue.text: The character to lie about ?

parts.note: to tell a small untruth is to fib
re is Latin-derived shorthand for concerning or on the subject of

explanation.surface: Someone asks what kind of person would tell untruths about another.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral fibre is a person's strength of character, so the word stands for character itself.

clue.text: Soho 14 ac mix-up, in a way

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so the letters of the two pieces are rearranged together

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 14 across, the gull's cry, mew

explanation.surface: A muddle in London's Soho district, of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district of central London. 'mix-up' shuffles SOHO with MEW, the answer to 14 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something somehow means doing it by some means or manner not specified.

clue.text: An Englishman does everything on this, said Shaw

definitions.text: An Englishman does everything on this, said Shaw

parts.words: An Englishman does everything on this, said Shaw
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Shaw's The Man of Destiny, where an Englishman is said to act on a fixed rule of conduct

explanation.surface: A quotation from George Bernard Shaw about English habits.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shaw's play The Man of Destiny, Napoleon says an Englishman 'does everything on principle', fighting, robbing or bullying alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a moral rule one claims to act by, which is the target of Shaw's gibe.

clue.text: Like part of a speech giving account, about troopship wreck

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the account abbreviation goes round the other piece
to wreck something is to break it up, so the letters of the ship are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speech recounting the wrecking of a military transport ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' makes POSTROPHI from TROOPSHIP, and 'about' puts the A and C of AC round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a rhetorical passage addressing someone absent, a part of a speech, and the adjective describes such a passage.

clue.text: Some of the etchings and so on

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: A list of some etchings and other artworks trailing off.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for et cetera means and the rest, so it stands for and so on.

clue.text: Army cover has diverted the final blow

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside from its course, so the letters of the short word are rearranged

parts.note: a knockout, KO, is the punch that ends a boxing bout

explanation.surface: A fighter's last punch was turned aside by a protective barrier of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' turns HAS into SHA, and KO, the knockout, follows. A shako is a tall peaked military hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall military cap with a plume, a headdress worn by soldiers, so an army head covering.

clue.text: In France a monkey gets treatment from a barber

explanation.surface: A monkey in France goes to the hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbers once singed hair ends with a taper to seal them.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for an ape or monkey is spelt the same as the English for a light burning, once given by barbers to hair ends.

clue.text: A short case — trouble with fruit

indicators.note: short means cut off, so only the first part of the grammatical word is kept

parts.note: the vocative is a grammatical case, used for addressing someone
ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A brief legal case over a dispute concerning fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is the grammatical case VOCATIVE, not a lawsuit; 'short' cuts it to VOC. The file held 'casetrouble' run together; the page prints a dash between.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Not as prescribed by Dr Voss (E. & O.E.) perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given may be arranged another way

parts.note: the letter E as printed
the letters O and E as printed

explanation.surface: A doctor named Voss signs a prescription with the business disclaimer for errors and omissions excepted.
explanation.walkthrough: E. & O.E. is the invoice formula 'errors and omissions excepted'; the ampersand is only a link. 'perhaps' shuffles DRVOSS with E, O and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdoses are excessive amounts of a drug, beyond what a doctor ordered; the definition describes them rather than replacing the noun exactly.

clue.text: The child's a little dear, say ? Afraid not

parts.note: Disney's Bambi is a little deer, and deer is said the same as dear
afraid not is a polite way of saying no

explanation.surface: Asked whether the child is a little darling, someone politely says no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: the little dear stands for a little deer, the fawn Bambi. Bambino is Italian for a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is an Italian word for a baby or young boy, used in English for a small child.

clue.text: Comfort for an organist

explanation.surface: Someone offers solace to a church musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe in sorrow is to console; an organ's keyboards, stops and pedals sit in the console where the organist plays.

clue.text: Hi! With 5 around, what singular morals !

indicators.note: with the other answer around it, the greeting sits inside

parts.note: the answer to 5 down, the abbreviation for et cetera
taken as written

explanation.surface: A greeting followed by an exclamation of shock at someone's odd morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With 5 around' puts the answer to 5 down, ETC, round HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are a set of moral principles; the singular form names one such moral code.

clue.text: Level up, geographically

parts.note: describes ground that is flat but raised high, as a geographer would label it

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like a call to raise one's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a broad flat area of high ground, level land lifted up.

clue.text: Management not barefaced enough to use this in building

parts.note: beaver is old slang for a beard, so someone with one is not barefaced
a board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: Executives too timid to put a certain material into construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barefaced' suggests boldness, but read it literally: a beaver is a beard, an old slang term.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaverboard is a fibreboard sheet material used for walls and ceilings in construction.

clue.text: Cry of the kittiwake, or gull ?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a seabird's cry is.
explanation.definitionFit: A mew is a thin high cry made by gulls and cats, and is also an old name for a seagull.

clue.text: Yet might one hold a candle to one who is this ?

definitions.text: Yet might one hold a candle to one who is this

parts.words: Yet might one hold a candle to one who is this
parts.note: plays on hold a candle to, meaning to compare with, while a candle needs lighting with something to strike

explanation.surface: Wondering whether anyone could compare with an unrivalled person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fit to hold a candle to' means far inferior to, so an unrivalled person has nobody who can; yet without a lighting stick a candle could be held to them anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peerless has no equal, so nothing can be set against it in comparison.

clue.text: Scatter sand on crops ? There are arguments on both sides

indicators.note: to scatter is to throw about loosely, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to spread grit over a field, with debate over the merits.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers the points for and against a proposal, the case each side puts.

clue.text: She took Scott to make his

definitions.text: She took Scott to make his

parts.words: She took Scott to make his
parts.note: the she is a ship, which carried the polar explorer Scott on his first Antarctic expedition, and the word also names what an explorer makes

explanation.surface: A woman carried the explorer Scott so he could make his name.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships are called 'she'. Scott's first Antarctic expedition (1901-04) sailed in the RRS of that name, and an explorer goes out to make finds.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship that carried Scott south, and the act of finding something new, share one name.

clue.text: Hip leaders call for them

parts.note: a cheerleader's cry of hip hip leads a crowd into rousing shouts of hooray

explanation.surface: Trendy bosses demand something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' looks like trendy, but it is the cry 'hip hip!' that leads into 'hooray!', three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader calls hip hip and a crowd answers hooray, repeated thrice as an acclamation.

clue.text: It was vexing the way the row was conducted

parts.note: a rank is a line or row of soldiers or taxis
led means guided or conducted

explanation.surface: Annoyance at the way a quarrel was handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: When something rankles it causes lasting irritation; the past form says the thing was irritating.

clue.text: Stepfathers ?

parts.note: split into step and fathers: the French word for a dance step, and a plural of the childish word for father

explanation.surface: Men who married into a family.
explanation.walkthrough: A pas is a step in ballet (pas de deux), and the same letters are the plural of 'pa'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballet term for a step and the plural of a familiar word for dad are spelt alike.

clue.text: For six thus it's a condition

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
VI is six in Roman numerals
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A rule saying that, for six people, there is a stipulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a clause in an agreement that sets a stipulation or requirement.

clue.text: Carroll's aged man sometimes searched "the grassy knolls for wheels of ——"

definitions.text: Carroll's aged man sometimes searched "the grassy knolls for wheels of ——"

parts.words: Carroll's aged man sometimes searched "the grassy knolls for wheels of ——"
parts.note: a gap-fill from the White Knight's song in Through the Looking-Glass, about an aged aged man

explanation.surface: A line of Lewis Carroll's nonsense verse with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: In the White Knight's song the aged man 'sometimes searched the grassy knolls for wheels of hansom-cabs'; the page prints the gap with a plural s.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, named after its designer Joseph Hansom, fills the verse's gap.

clue.text: Highlights of a gold particle

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: The best bits of a speck of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlights' is the definition: the constellation's bright stars, such as Betelgeuse and Rigel, are lights high in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a bright constellation, a group of shining stars high in the night sky.

clue.text: Part of the seaside atmosphere?

parts.note: the bracing smell of the coast was popularly credited to a form of oxygen in the air

explanation.surface: Something that makes up the feel of a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ozone' of seaside air was once thought to be what made sea air healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen with three atoms was popularly thought to give sea air its tang.

clue.text: Permission to leave the river doesn't say where

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
at is a preposition of place that, standing alone, names no place

explanation.surface: Permission is given to leave a river with no destination named.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe runs through Devon to Exeter. 'At' alone is a word of place with no place after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is leave of absence granted to a pupil at a boarding school or college.

clue.text: Bogy-man of Goethe's forest

parts.note: points to the evil spirit of the woods in Goethe's ballad, set by Schubert

explanation.surface: A monster from a German poet's woods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Goethe's poem a malevolent spirit of the forest lures a child to death, a figure of German folklore.

clue.text: Stop someone telling a joke, either way

explanation.surface: Silencing someone mid-joke, from either end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either way' adds that the three letters read the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To muzzle a person stops them speaking; a comedian's quip is also called by the same short word.

clue.text: Does mine hostess drink like a fish?

definitions.text: Does mine hostess drink like a fish?

parts.words: Does mine hostess drink like a fish?
parts.note: the landlady of an alehouse, and a fish of the herring family, share one name

explanation.surface: Asking whether the landlady of the inn is a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine host' is the landlord of an inn; the alewife was a woman who kept an alehouse, and an alewife is also a North American fish of the herring family.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a woman running an alehouse and a herring-like fish.

clue.text: Something wicked holding a party with old port ?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a sin is a wicked act
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Wicked goings-on at a party, with a bottle of vintage fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is a harbour town, not a wine: Sidon is an ancient Phoenician port in Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidon was a great harbour city of ancient Phoenicia.

clue.text: Billy has vertigo

parts.note: a billy is a male goat, and having vertigo makes one dizzy

explanation.surface: A boy named Billy suffers from dizziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billy' looks like a name but is a billy goat, and vertigo makes it giddy. To play the giddy goat is to fool about.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing the giddy goat is an idiom for behaving foolishly, a dizzy male farm animal.
